evidence: The round-0 hunk gates warnings on `len(r.Warnings) > 0 && len(r.Errors) == 0`, hiding warnings whenever errors exist; the 7a61c11 diff shows `if len(r.Warnings) > 0 {` with the guard gone, matching the reply.
guidance_note: When a report struct carries independent Errors and Warnings slices, render each section unconditionally on its own length rather than making one section's visibility depend on the other.

evidence: Every write in formatDoctorReport is `_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(...)` and the function returns nil, so a failed stdout write exits 0 while the old one-line Fprintf returned its err. The 7a61c11 diff still has the discarded writes; the claimed fix commit is not in the packet, and the PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: When replacing a single error-returning Fprintf with a multi-line formatter, keep the same contract by threading each write's error, or by writing to a buffer and returning one write error.

evidence: The reply says 'We don't assert on exact CLI text formatting in this project', but the errors+warnings case the reviewer listed is exactly F1's hidden-warnings bug, and other PRs in this repo (#52 ready_test.go text-output tests, #62 help-text assertions) do assert on text output. Snapshot tests are a preference, but a test that warnings appear alongside errors checks behavior.
guidance_note: When adding a formatter with branches on report contents, test each branch combination (none, errors only, warnings only, both) for which sections appear, not for exact whitespace.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the round-0 hunk at 9503bba already printed 'Run `lit fsck --repair`' and the round-0 summary already describes the fsck --repair prefix, so 7a61c11 only re-carries pre-review logic. The finding is real (fsck --repair tells the user to run fsck --repair), and classifying issues as auto-fixable is a sound data-driven cure.
guidance_note: When one formatter serves two commands, check every hard-coded hint line against each caller, especially the caller that is the hint's own target.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the formatDoctorReport header lines are unchanged from the round-0 code. The reply says doctor JSON and exit codes are covered by integration tests, but the packet shows no such test, so whether `doctor --json` stability is pinned cannot be checked.

narrative: Copilot raised a real hidden-warnings bug, ignored write errors, and a self-referential repair hint; the agent fixed or redesigned each. Both test-coverage requests were declined with a 'we don't test CLI text' convention that the F1 bug undercuts. Rounds 2-6 are reply-only elton-prawn entries with no findings, and the PR was closed unmerged after conflicting with #53.
guidance_observations: The round-1 findings were flagged ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT only because the commit was rewritten; none of them came from a review fix.
The convention against testing CLI text was stated as a blanket rule and used to decline behavioral tests that would have caught the PR's own bug.

evidence: Go does not reject unused function parameters, so 'compile error' is false; but `format` really is unread in printReadySection, which is the symptom of F2. Removing it alongside the --format flag is the right cleanup.
guidance_note: When a rewrite stops reading a parameter, delete the parameter and the flag that feeds it in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk renders a fixed numbered layout regardless of `format` while `runReady` still advertised `--format lines|table`. Removing the flag entirely beats the reviewer's suggestion to restore a table mode the new design does not want.
guidance_note: When replacing an output mode, grep for the flag's registration and help text and remove the advertisement in the same change.

narrative: One round with two linked findings: the renderer rewrite left the `format` parameter and the `--format` flag dangling. The agent removed both in dac2911. The reviewer's compile-error claim was wrong, but it pointed at the real dead flag.
guidance_observations: Both findings come from one omission: the rewrite did not trace the flag it stopped honoring back to its registration.

evidence: fixAllPriorityPullForward shares one `visited` map across all roots, so a blocker visited first as its own root is skipped when a later higher-priority dependent's traversal reaches it. The bug class is real, but the reviewer's example contradicts its own ordering claim: in_progress sorts before open, so the dependent would be processed first. The thread is resolved and outdated with no reply, so the packet does not show whether it was fixed.
guidance_note: When lifting a single-root traversal into a loop over many roots, give each root its own cycle-detection set unless shared state is keyed by the strongest constraint seen.

evidence: The batch tests shown create only all-open issues, so ordering-dependent misses from F1 go untested. There is no reply; the thread was resolved, and #54 removed fix-priority entirely about four hours later, which may have made the test moot.
guidance_note: When a batch algorithm's correctness depends on iteration order, write one test whose fixture puts the dependency before the dependent in that order.

narrative: One review flagged a plausible shared-visited-map traversal bug and a matching test gap. Neither thread got a reply. The PR merged 21 minutes after the review, and the command was removed in #54 the same morning.
guidance_observations: Resolving threads with no reply leaves no record of whether a correctness finding was fixed or dismissed.

evidence: The comment says 'dependency (src) is ranked below the dependent (dst)', but FixRankInversions' own struct labels dependentID as 'src in blocks relation'. The PR merged at 09:33, before the 09:37 review; the same backwards comment was re-shipped in #55 (F2) and only fixed in #56.
guidance_note: When writing a SQL comment about relation direction, copy the src/dst roles from the one place that defines them, here the inversion struct's field comments.

evidence: RankAbove calls `s.GetIssue(ctx, targetID)` before acquiring the lock and transaction, then computes a midpoint against `target.Rank`, so a concurrent re-rank makes that read stale. The PR merged before the review, and no later packet in this batch shows the read moved inside the transaction.
guidance_note: When a mutation computes a new value from another row's value, read that row inside the same locked transaction that writes.

evidence: The loop calls `s.RankAbove` per inversion, and each RankAbove does its own tx, commitWorkingSet and smoothing, giving one Dolt commit per inversion. #56 later batched it into one transaction.
guidance_note: When a repair loop reuses a public mutation method, check whether that method commits, and batch under one lock and commit when it does.

evidence: `issueRank := in.Rank` is inserted unvalidated; Midpoint does return 'rank: invalid character' errors, so later operations fail rather than panic, which makes 'even panic' overstated. Persisting an invalid rank at the import boundary is still a real gap.
guidance_note: When a new column has a constrained alphabet, validate it at every write path that accepts it from outside, import included.

evidence: RankBelow repeats RankAbove's pattern of `s.GetIssue(ctx, targetID)` before the transaction. The same pre-lock read as F2 is in the sibling method of the same diff, not a fix-caused instance. The PR merged before review.
guidance_note: When writing paired Above/Below methods, write one helper that reads the target inside the transaction and call it from both.

evidence: Tracing the hunk: Midpoint('A','A0') emits 'A', then at i=1 the virtual aChar 0 equals real '0', so it emits '0', then 'V', giving 'A0V' > 'A0'. No string lies strictly between 'A' and 'A0', so the real cure is never generating ranks that end in the minimum digit. #57 later fixed related spacing panics.
guidance_note: When writing fractional indexing, use a virtual floor below the real alphabet minimum and add a property test that Midpoint(a,b) lies strictly between a and b for random pairs, including prefix pairs.

evidence: The diff literally changes `doctor fsck backup` to `doctorbackup` in the fish list. The bug was re-shipped in #55 (F4) and fixed in #56.
guidance_note: When deleting a word from a space-separated command list, add a test that every registered subcommand appears as its own token in each completion script.

evidence: The bash `local commands=` line has the same `doctorbackup` concatenation as the fish list, from the same edit. The bug was re-shipped in #55 (F6) and fixed in #56.
guidance_note: When editing one of several parallel completion lists, generate them from the registered command set rather than hand-editing each string.

narrative: The PR merged 4 minutes after creation, before Copilot's review landed. All eight findings went unanswered: a backwards comment, two stale pre-lock reads, per-inversion commits, unvalidated import ranks, a genuine Midpoint contract violation, and two doctorbackup typos. #55 re-shipped most of them and #56 fixed only a subset.
guidance_observations: Merging before the review lands turned every finding into follow-up PR work and left real bugs (stale reads, Midpoint prefix case) with no recorded disposition.
The doctorbackup typo in two hand-maintained lists shows a missing completion-vs-registry test.

evidence: `fn(ctx, stdout, ap)` lets fixes write progress to stdout before printValue emits the JSON report, so `doctor --fix --json` emits mixed text and JSON. #56's summary says fix progress was routed to stderr.
guidance_note: When a command supports --json, route every non-payload line (progress, notices) to stderr from the first version.

evidence: This is the same backwards src/dst comment already flagged as #54/F1 an hour earlier, re-shipped unfixed in this PR. It is a repeat of an ignored finding, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: Before opening a follow-up PR over code that already drew findings, clear or explicitly dispose of those findings first.

evidence: This is the per-inversion RankAbove loop with one commit each, the same as #54/F3 and still unfixed here. #56 batched it, and that batch dropped smoothing (#56/F2).
guidance_note: Before opening a follow-up PR over code that already drew findings, clear or explicitly dispose of those findings first.

evidence: The fish list still contains `doctorbackup`, already flagged as #54/F7; fixed in #56.
guidance_note: Before opening a follow-up PR over code that already drew findings, clear or explicitly dispose of those findings first.

evidence: The hunk renames resolveFsckAccessMode to resolveDoctorAccessMode with NoOptDefVal semantics, while the reviewer notes its test was deleted. #56 touches app_bootstrap_test and adds `--json` handling to doctor access-mode resolution, which suggests the gap was real.
guidance_note: When renaming a function that had a unit test, port the test to the new name and new flag semantics rather than deleting it.

evidence: The bash list still contains `doctorbackup`, already flagged as #54/F8; fixed in #56.
guidance_note: Before opening a follow-up PR over code that already drew findings, clear or explicitly dispose of those findings first.

narrative: A superset of #54 opened 49 minutes after it merged. It carried four of #54's unanswered findings forward verbatim (comment direction, per-inversion commits, two doctorbackup typos) and added a JSON-corruption bug and a deleted access-mode test. No replies; the PR was closed and the fixes landed in #56.
guidance_observations: The one review round is avoidable: four of its six findings were already-known bugs from #54 that the agent re-shipped without fixing.
Two PRs in a row authored as elton-prawn got no thread replies at all, so nothing records why any finding was accepted or dropped.

evidence: Inversions are captured once and each iteration moves the dependency to just above its dependent; with one blocker over dependents at ranks 5 and 10, the second move places it near 10, above the first dependent again. The per-inversion RankAbove loop in #54/#55 had the same semantics, so batching did not cause this. #60 exists to fix it.
guidance_note: When repairing order violations from a snapshot, group by the moved item and target the strictest constraint, or loop until the inversion query returns zero.

evidence: The old loop went through RankAbove, which ends in `s.smoothRanksIfNeeded(ctx, newRank)`; the batched rewrite answering #54/F3/#55/F3 inlines the midpoint and update but drops the smoothing call. Unanswered here, it was re-raised as #60/F3.
guidance_note: When inlining a method into a batch loop, list every side effect the method performed (commit, smoothing, timestamps) and carry each one over or delete it deliberately.

evidence: `dep add` accepts `--type blocks|parent-child|related-to`, but the new output hard-codes `--depends-on-->` for every type, mislabeling related-to and parent-child edges. #59 later reworked dep output for the blocks type only.
guidance_note: When relabeling output for one enum value, branch on that value so the other values keep their own label.

evidence: `dep ls` got the same unconditional `--depends-on-->` replacement as `dep add` in the same diff. It is a sibling of F3 introduced in the same commit, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When the same relation is rendered in two subcommands, put the arrow text in one function keyed on relation type and call it from both.

narrative: This PR cleared the carried-over #54/#55 findings (comment direction, completion typos, stderr progress, batching). The batching rewrite dropped rank smoothing, and the snapshot-based repair still could not converge for shared blockers. It merged 4 minutes after creation, before the review; the convergence bug became #60 and the smoothing gap was re-flagged there.
guidance_observations: The third consecutive merge-before-review: the smoothing regression from this PR's own fix went unanswered and cost a later round in #60.
The batching fix inlined RankAbove without auditing what RankAbove did beyond the update.

evidence: With `denominator := big.NewInt(int64(n + 1))`, n=-1 gives a zero divisor (big.Int Div panics), and n<-1 gives a negative step that never terminates the length search. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply implemented exactly the suggested guard.
guidance_note: When converting arithmetic to big.Int with a new error return, validate every integer input's domain at the same boundary.

evidence: upperBoundInt returns stringToInt(s,length)-1, and an all-'0' upper pads to 0, so the bound is -1 at every length and the spacing loop never finds room. The agent added the Sign()==0 rejection plus TestSpacedRanksBetweenRejectsZeroUpperBound.
guidance_note: When a loop grows a parameter until a span becomes positive, prove the span can become positive for every input, or bound the loop and error.

narrative: One review found two non-termination or panic inputs in the new big.Int spacing code. The agent accepted both with targeted guards and regression tests. The reply-hint labels were misleading: both replies were acceptances.
guidance_observations: The agent replied on each thread and posted test evidence, which is a clean contrast with the merge-before-review PRs #54-#56.

evidence: The finding cites a later 'Machine-readable mode' section that recommends --json, but the packet's hunk shows only lines 5-10 of agent-workflow.md, so the contradiction cannot be confirmed. The PR merged 1 minute after creation, before the review.
guidance_note: When removing a flag from a doc's example, grep the same doc for general advice about that flag.

evidence: The removed warning existed because `--json` output tempted agents to jq out bare IDs; with text-mode `lit ready` that hazard is gone, so re-adding the guardrail is a preference, not a gap. The right answer was a one-line pushback, not silence on an unresolved thread.
This is F2 again on the generated AGENTS.md mirror, with the same reasoning: the removed ID-extraction warning was specific to JSON output, which the PR stopped recommending.

narrative: A docs-only PR dropping `lit ready --json` from agent guidance. It merged 1 minute after creation, before Copilot posted. One finding about a possibly contradictory machine-readable section cannot be checked from the packet; the other two ask to restore a warning whose reason the PR removed.
guidance_observations: Merging before review left three threads unresolved with no recorded disposition, including one that may be a real doc contradiction.

evidence: The reviewer quotes a zero-arg usage string `lit dep <add|rm> ...` and a default branch with `<add|rm|ls>`, but the hunk shows neither line, so the packet cannot confirm the mismatch. The PR merged 4 minutes after creation, 41 seconds before the review.

narrative: This PR fixed blocks-direction rendering in dep commands, partly answering #56/F3-F4. The single cosmetic usage-string finding arrived after merge and got no reply.
guidance_observations: Another merge seconds before the review landed; the finding is minor but has no disposition.

evidence: The shared clause filters only `status != 'closed'`, while the neighbor query in the same function uses `deleted_at IS NULL`, so deleted rows could drive detection and repair. The predicate was missing from the original #54 inversion query too, so this is not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When extracting a shared SQL clause for one scope, compare its visibility predicates against every other query on the same table in the function.

evidence: The return changed from `len(inversions)` to `totalFixed`, which counts dependency updates, while the docs and output still said inversions. The agent took the reviewer's option (1) and renamed the contract to issues re-ranked.
guidance_note: When changing what a returned count measures, update its docstring and every message that prints it in the same commit.

evidence: This is the smoothing call dropped when #56 inlined RankAbove to batch FixRankInversions (answering #54/F3 and #55/F3). It was already flagged as #56/F2 and ignored, then finally fixed here with smoothRanksIfNeededTx.
guidance_note: When inlining a method into a batch loop, list every side effect the method performed and carry each over; and answer a regression finding on the PR that introduced it.

narrative: This PR fixed #56/F1's non-convergence by iterating FixRankInversions to a fixpoint. Copilot found a missing deleted_at filter, a count-semantics drift, and the smoothing call still missing from the #56 batching rewrite. The agent fixed all three with tests in a6689a0.
guidance_observations: F3 is a cross-PR cost: a regression flagged on #56 and ignored there resurfaced as a finding on this PR.

evidence: The new code comment says guidance loads from 'the managed AGENTS template' while the code loads `templates.QuickstartTemplateName`; the agent corrected the comment.
guidance_note: When writing a comment that names the data source, copy the identifier the code actually passes.

evidence: Removing `fs.Bool("json", ...)` made `lit quickstart --json` an unknown-flag error with a different exit category. The agent added the hidden shim flag the reviewer suggested, then removed it in 524bd68 as mode accumulation, which reopened the issue as F3; its own later root fix (unknown flag maps to ExitUsage in exit.go) was the right answer here.
guidance_note: When a reviewer proposes a per-command shim for an error-classification inconsistency, look for the single place errors are classified and fix it there for every command.

evidence: The agent added the F2 shim, then deliberately removed it in 524bd68, which brought the unknown-flag behavior back; the reply verifies the exit codes differ (ExitUsage vs ExitGeneric). Mapping 'unknown flag' to ExitUsage in ExitCode() fixes every command with no hidden flag, which matches no-mode-explosion.
guidance_note: When reverting a review fix, re-check the finding it answered and land the replacement cure in the same push.

narrative: Round 0 found a stale comment and the unknown-flag regression from dropping quickstart's --json. The agent applied the reviewer's shim, later removed it without replacing it, and round 1 re-raised the same issue. Two weeks later the agent fixed it at the root in exit.go.
guidance_observations: Round 1 is avoidable: had the first answer to F2 been the global exit-code mapping, there would have been no shim to revert and nothing to re-raise.
A deliberate revert of a review fix should be paired with its replacement before pushing, not left for the reviewer to rediscover.

evidence: The test asserts `"ready       List open..."` with literal padding, which shifts whenever the longest command name changes, and the same file already has normalizeWhitespace for this purpose. The thread is resolved and outdated with no reply, so the packet does not show whether the test was normalized.
guidance_note: When asserting on aligned help output, reuse the file's existing whitespace normalizer instead of hard-coding padding.

narrative: One valid brittleness finding on a new help-text test, with a ready fix (normalizeWhitespace) already in the same file. The thread was resolved with no reply and later went outdated.
guidance_observations: The new test ignored a helper sitting a few lines above it that solves exactly this problem.

evidence: It is true that `--status=` now yields the default open/in_progress filter, but an empty status value is not narrowing by status, which is what the code comment says. Relying on `--status=` to mean 'all statuses' was never a documented path. The pushback is defensible, though 'no thanks' records no reasoning.

The PR is +6/-0 in one file with no test, and it changes the default visible set of `lit ls`, a user-facing contract. A JSON-mode test that the default excludes closed and that `--status closed` and `--query status:closed` include it is cheap and behavioral.
guidance_note: When changing a command's default filter, add a test pinning the default and each override path in the same PR.

narrative: A six-line default-filter change. The empty-`--status` edge case was reasonably declined, though only with 'no thanks'. The request for a default/override test went unanswered, and the PR merged nine days later without one.
guidance_observations: A one-word pushback leaves the next reader to rediscover why the edge case was acceptable.

evidence: The store validation `if reason == "" { return ... "reason is required" }` was deleted with no test of the newly legal input. The agent added TestTransitionIssueAllowsEmptyReason with a GetIssueDetail round-trip in d36b94c.
guidance_note: When relaxing a validation, add a test that the formerly rejected input now succeeds end to end.

evidence: The deleted check `if strings.TrimSpace(*reason) == "" { return errors.New("--reason is required") }` lived in runBulk, so the store-level test cannot catch it coming back. The 'we don't assert on CLI text' rationale does not apply to a test asserting success and transitioned state.
guidance_note: When a validation is removed from two layers, test each layer, because a lower-layer test cannot see a guard re-added above it.

evidence: The agent itself enumerated the stale `--reason <text>` usage strings at cli.go:996, :2909-2910 and the quickstart examples, and updated them to `[--reason <text>]` in d36b94c.
guidance_note: When making a flag optional, grep for the flag name across usage strings, help, and examples before opening the PR.

narrative: Making transition reason optional drew three findings: two test gaps and stale usage text. The agent fixed the store test and the docs in one commit. It declined the CLI-layer test on a redundancy argument that does not hold for a guard removed from the CLI layer itself.
guidance_observations: The usage-string drift was found by the reviewer but fully enumerated by the agent, which means a pre-PR grep for the flag would have caught it.
